desc: **Task 1 (math spec):** GF(2) reduction — A ⇒ `h_j=h_{j-1}^1, v_i=v_{i-1}^1`; B ⇒ `h_j=h_{j-1}, v_i=v_{i-1}, h^v=1`; free vars `r_i,c_j`; every row/column needs an even number of `A`; each B cell gives edge `r_i^c_j = 1^P[i][j]^Q[i][j]`; answer `0` on parity fail / odd-weight cycle, else `2^C` with C = #components on H+W nodes (isolated included). Samples: 2, 0, 2 ✔

**Task 2 (implementation):** End-to-end script — bulk parse, global row prefix XOR + row parity, W-grouped column prefix XOR + column parity, global disjoint node ids, B-cell edge extraction, scipy doubled-node `connected_components` primary engine with pure-Python parity-DSU fallback, per-test component counts via `reduceat`/`bincount`, vectorized two-table `2^C`, single write.

**Task 3 (correctness cross-check):** Model re-derived independently (wrap conventions, bijectivity of orientation↔edge-values for both tile types); hand-enumerated 2×2 all-A (16), 2×2 all-B (2), 2×3 `AAB/AAB` (8), 2×4 `ABBA/ABBA` (8), plus all three provided samples — all match. Both connectivity engines traced line-by-line and shown to agree in `counts`/`conflict` semantics.

**Task 4 (performance reasoning):** No per-test NumPy calls; only Python-level loops are parsing (O(T)) and the distinct-`W` group loop (O(√ΣHW) ≈ ≤10³ iterations). Graph has ≤2·10⁶ edges handled in one scipy C call; peak memory ≈80 MB at ΣHW = 10⁶.
**Task 5 (fallback):** Pure-Python inlined parity DSU retained as scipy-free path; deemed sufficient (judges with NumPy ship SciPy), no further engine needed.
